source.title: Homological stability for Hurwitz spaces and the Cohen-Lenstra conjecture over function fields
source.authors: Jordan S. Ellenberg, Akshay Venkatesh and Craig Westerland
readSections: Complete published paper: introduction §§1.1–1.11, §§2–8, every displayed proof, Table 1 and references; extracted text lines 1–2734.
Rendered printed pp.733,739,763,772,774,777,779 checked against extraction; other displayed expressions checked in text.
Codex codex-c83e7a continuation,2026-09-23: read all58 published PDF pages729–786; independently checked the exact-family monodromy invocation and inherited moment-convergence witness.

summary: Nonsplitting finite-group Hurwitz spaces admit linear-range homological stabilization by a central sum of gluing operators. Tame comparison gives exponential uniform Betti bounds, and symplectic monodromy plus trace/weight estimates gives Cohen–Lenstra surjection moments and large-q limits of degree-density liminf/sup. No fixed-q distribution limit or Frobenius-equivariant stabilization is proved. This checkpoint includes a replacement proof of the enlargement counting step, explicit source findings and finite regression witnesses, but retains recursive source and general noncommutative-Tor ownership gaps. Continuation: supplies an explicit labelled quotient-stack comparison for the monic polynomial family, with the connected lifted affine group and retained deck involution; verifies the integral lifting reference in the g≥2 range needed for eventual n, records its g=1,ell=3 exception, and corrects the predecessor probability witness to an elementary abelian group. Status remains partial because recursive suppliers remain open.
conventions: Unless an item specifies otherwise, §§3–6 use finite G, one conjugacy class c generating G and satisfying nonsplitting, and a field k with |G| invertible. g^h=h^{-1}gh.
Graded modules are nonnegatively graded; degree is the supremum of nonzero degrees with explicit bottom for zero and infinity for unbounded modules. M[q]_n=M_(n−q), zero for n<q.

Arithmetic conclusions in this checkpoint require q odd, ell an odd prime, ell not dividing q(q−1), and A a finite abelian ell-group. Distinguish the statistical prime ell from the auxiliary etale coefficient prime L.
All library claims concern only the displayed generic carrier/theorem, not the EVW-specific adapter. All API names are planning names, not existing Lean declarations.

items.name: Singular chain and homology functors
items.statement: For a coefficient object in a preadditive category with coproducts, singular chains are obtained from the singular simplicial set; when homology exists, singular homology is a functor of spaces.

items.name: Artin braid group carrier
items.statement: The n-strand braid group is the Artin group of the A_(n−1) Coxeter matrix, with n−1 generators, adjacent braid relations and distant commutation; its universal map is determined by images satisfying those relations.

items.name: Conjugation quandle
items.statement: For a group G, the conjugation quandle operation is x ◃ y = xyx^{-1}. This is the positive Hurwitz-move operation, whereas EVW's exponent notation is g^h=h^{-1}gh.

items.name: Monoid algebra carrier
items.statement: For a semiring k and monoid S, MonoidAlgebra k S consists of finitely supported k-coefficients with convolution. For commutative k and a k-algebra B, monoid maps S→B extend uniquely to algebra maps.

items.name: Spectral sequence carrier
items.statement: In an abelian category C, a spectral sequence with chosen complex shapes consists of pages and specified identifications of each page's homology with the next page; this alone supplies no filtration, convergence or EVW differential.

items.name: Semidirect product carrier
items.statement: Given groups N,H and an action H→Aut(N), SemidirectProduct N H has multiplication (n,h)(n',h')=(n·h(n'),hh'), canonical inclusions and quotient to H.

items.name: Symplectic matrix carrier
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and finite index set I, symplecticGroup I R comprises matrices preserving the standard alternating matrix J by A J Aᵀ=J. No general GSp multiplier-orbit theorem is included in this claim.

items.name: Finite-cell exponential bound
items.statement: Conf_n has a CW model with at most 2^n cells. Its finite cover Hur^c has a model with at most (2|G|)^n cells, hence every Betti number over any field is at most (2|G|)^n.

items.name: Hyperelliptic boundary degeneration input

items.name: Overlapping symplectic subgroups generate
items.statement: In the setting of Achter–Pries Lemma 3.1, the two symplectic block subgroups obtained from the overlapping genus decompositions generate the full finite symplectic group. Together with the genus-one and genus-two base cases this gives full mod-ell hyperelliptic monodromy.

items.name: Integral lift of full mod-ell monodromy
items.statement: Let H be a closed subgroup of Sp_(2g)(Z_ell), ell odd, surjecting onto Sp_(2g)(F_ell). Then H is the whole group if g≥2 or ell≥5. For g=1,ell=3, Vasiu1.3(b) requires H mod9 to intersect the first congruence kernel nontrivially. Surjectivity modulo3 alone is insufficient: the inverse image of the order24 subgroup of SL2(Z/9) generated by [[0,1],[8,0]] and [[1,7],[6,7]] is a proper closed subgroup of index27 that still surjects modulo3.
items.proofOutline: Sp is simply connected, so c(G)=1. For ell≥5 use1.3(a); for ell=3,g≥2 no normal algebraic SL2 or PGL2 factor exists, so1.3(b) has no extra condition. The image of a profinite fundamental group is compact, hence closed. The proof uses irreducibility of the adjoint module, nonsplitting of reduction modulo ell², and congruence-power lifting. Selected original statements and proofs were read; their remaining root-system/representation-theory prerequisites are explicit recursive gaps.

items.name: Universal-coefficient dimension comparison
items.statement: For the proper finiteness hypotheses on geometric etale cohomology used in Proposition 7.8, rational L-adic Betti dimension is at most the number of generators of integral cohomology, which is at most mod-L cohomology dimension by the universal-coefficient sequence. This is a rank inequality, not a mod-L/rational isomorphism.

items.proofOutline: Etale locally choose a coordinate on the genus-zero quotient taking the last label to infinity, and a frame of the trace-zero line bundle. The branch equation is lambda prod(x−a_i); adjoining a square root of the unit lambda makes it monic. A cover isomorphism preserving infinity has x′=ax+b; equivariance under the involution forces y′=dy, with d²=a^n. Conversely each such triple defines an isomorphism, and its composition law is B_n. This proves local essential surjectivity and the Isom-sheaf identity, hence the stack equivalence by descent.

items.name: Connected smooth torsors preserve the full fundamental-group image
items.statement: For a connected locally noetherian DM stack X and a representable smooth surjection f:U→X with geometrically connected nonempty fibres, U is connected and pi1(U)→pi1(X) is surjective. In particular this holds for a torsor under a smooth geometrically connected group.
items.locator: Finite-cover proof supplied in report; extends IG.0 within the stack range
items.proofOutline: For a connected finite etale cover Y→X, the base change U_Y→Y is smooth, surjective and has connected fibres. A nontrivial clopen partition of U_Y would have disjoint open images in Y, because each connected fibre lies wholly in one member. These images partition Y, a contradiction. Apply the finite-cover image criterion; apply the same argument to Y=X for connectedness of U.

items.name: Restriction to the smooth hyperelliptic locus preserves monodromy

Apply this to the smooth-curve locus inside the compact-type locus on which AP defines the Jacobian abelian scheme; its mod-ell and ell-adic monodromy image is unchanged.
items.locator: AP§3.1 definition of monodromy on S* and Theorem3.4; explicit restriction lemma
items.proofOutline: A connected finite etale cover of a normal locally noetherian stack is normal and irreducible. Its pullback to the dense open is nonempty irreducible, hence connected. Use the image criterion. AP smoothness and irreducibility apply to the labelled base; no assertion is made that Pic^0 is abelian over every nodal stable curve.

items.proofOutline: Base genera1,2 use full curve-moduli monodromy and the lack of a common nontrivial quotient of Sym(2g+2) and Sp_(2g)(F_ell). For g≥3 use the1,g−2,1 compact-type degeneration and the two overlapping symplectic subgroups. items.name: Finite torsion-level monodromy in the exact polynomial family
items.statement: In the range of item116, for each k≥1 the geometric image on the Jacobian ell^k-torsion is Sp_(2g)(Z/ell^k). The integral symplectic group surjects to every finite level by smoothness, and the representation is the reduction of the integral Tate-module representation.
items.proofOutline: Use full integral image, the identification T_ell/ell^k≃Jac[ell^k], and surjectivity of reduction. This statement does not identify the unmarked Hurwitz fibre with the marked surjection set; its sign quotient remains item97/E10.

items.name: Trace-zero normal form for a branched double cover
items.statement: With2 invertible, a finite flat degree2 cover is locally the algebra O⊕L^(-1), where L is a line bundle and multiplication on the trace-zero summand is a section s of L². In the smooth hyperelliptic case the reduced branch divisor is div(s). Over a labelled genus-zero quotient with a distinguished branch section, etale-local trivializations yield y²=lambda prod(x−a_i), with lambda a unit and infinity the remaining branch point.
items.locator: Underlying cover algebra for item131; imports line-bundle/curve foundations from SF.3
items.proofOutline: The trace divided by2 splits the unit summand. Cayley–Hamilton for a trace-zero element gives a scalar square, defining multiplication. Conversely the displayed rank2 algebra reconstructs the cover; basis changes give the line-bundle gluing. On P1 the branch degree2g+2 forces L to have relative degree g+1. Trivialize the base line-bundle factor locally and then take an etale square root of lambda. General relative Picard, genus-zero trivialization and descent remain supplier obligations.

items.name: Arithmetic monodromy quotient and the cyclotomic multiplier
items.statement: Let S be geometrically connected over F and let a principally polarized abelian scheme give arithmetic and geometric ell-adic images A and G. The multiplier induces an exact sequence 1→(A∩Sp)/G→A/G→chi_ell(G_F)→1. If G=Sp, the left kernel is trivial. Without this hypothesis A/G need not be the cyclotomic image.
items.locator: AP§3.1, PDF p.10; corrected input for EVW8.8 and AP Corollary3.6
items.proofOutline: Use the geometric/arithmetic fundamental-group sequence and compatibility of the Weil pairing with the cyclotomic character. Quotient A by G and take the kernel of the induced multiplier. For a counterexample to the unconditional claim, take S=Spec C(t) and the quadratic twist by t of a constant elliptic curve: G=1, A={±I}, and chi_ell=1 for ell odd.
